providers.name: Anoka County Lexington Avenue Rice Creek Water Trail access anchor
providers.method: Anoka County’s current Rice Creek Water Trail wayfinder map identifies Lexington Avenue as a public access point on the trail. Retain the route’s existing road/access-area pin; the map does not publish a surveyed water-entry coordinate. The offset may represent the access path or road approach, not an error to snap to the creek centerline.

controls.name: Lexington Avenue access
aliases: Rice Creek Water Trail Lexington access
controls.coordinateText: Route pin retained as an access-area anchor. The County map confirms a named Lexington Avenue access but publishes no exact coordinate or waterline point.

providers.name: NPS Paces Mill public canoe and raft launch access anchor
providers.method: The current NPS compendium lists Paces Mill as a public access launch ramp, and current NPS boating guidance includes Paces Mill among boat-access locations. Retain the existing site pin as a facility/access-area anchor; NPS does not publish a machine-readable ramp-toe coordinate on these pages. An NPS project closure ran October 2024 through May 2025; current NPS access listings support the reopened site.

controls.name: Paces Mill Canoe and Raft Launch
controls.coordinateText: Existing route coordinate retained as a launch-facility anchor; NPS confirms the public launch but does not publish this coordinate as a surveyed ramp toe.

providers.name: Minnesota DNR Miller Landing Sauk River public water access feature
providers.method: Minnesota DNR public-water-access GIS feature OBJECTID 2504 / WAS00341 names the Sauk River Miller Landing Public Water Access Site, identifies Stearns County, gives the directions to the south bank, and lists river mile 7.6. Its WGS84 geometry is x=-94.26496023134358, y=45.55179577632979. Standardize route and trip-detail references to this official GIS access-site point; it is a site anchor, not a surveyed launch toe.

controls.name: Sauk River, Miller Landing Public Water Access Site
controls.coordinateText: Official GIS feature OBJECTID 2504 / WAS00341; ArcGIS x is longitude and y is latitude. DNR Map 2 identifies this as a right-bank carry-in at RM 7.6.

providers.name: BLM Murtaugh Snake River boating access anchor
providers.method: BLM identifies Murtaugh Boating Access as the put-in for the Murtaugh Snake River reach, describes class V opportunities when flows are sufficient, and gives directions five miles north of Murtaugh on Murtaugh Road. Retain the route’s existing site pin as an access anchor; the page does not publish an exact entry coordinate.

controls.name: Murtaugh Boating Access
controls.coordinateText: Existing route point retained for the BLM-named put-in site; no exact waterline coordinate is published.

providers.name: NPS Round Spring Current River floater landing area anchor
providers.method: The current NPS Superintendent’s Compendium lists Round Spring (middle) as a Current River landing for floaters and separately lists Round Spring Boat Ramp among launches dedicated to motorized vessels. Keep the stored campsite/area pin as a general Round Spring access anchor, not as the exact boat-ramp or floater-landing coordinate. Route notes should direct paddlers to the signed floater landing and not the motorized ramp.

controls.name: Round Spring Current River floater access area
aliases: Round Spring river access / campground area
controls.coordinateText: Stored point is an access/campground-area anchor; NPS distinguishes the floater landing from its separate motorized-only boat ramp and does not publish an exact coordinate for either feature here.

providers.name: Pennsylvania DCNR Lower Yough Ohiopyle launch access anchor
providers.method: Pennsylvania DCNR identifies the Lower Yough launch below Ohiopyle Falls, specifies that the put-in is river-right on the Ferncliff side and reached by Ferncliff Trail, and prohibits using this launch as the falls-run takeout. Retain the existing point as a launch-area anchor; DCNR does not publish a precise water-entry coordinate on the guidance page.

controls.name: Ohiopyle State Park Lower Yough launch
controls.coordinateText: Existing route point retained as a launch-area anchor; use the DCNR-marked river-right Ferncliff Trail entry downstream of the buoy line, not an assumed river-left entry.

providers.name: Taylors Falls Lions Park South St. Croix access and dam-portage anchor
providers.method: The City of Taylors Falls identifies Lions Park South—not Lions Park North—as the St. Croix bank park with a boat launch. The current NPS St. Croix map directs paddlers on the upstream reach to portage right at Taylors Falls Lion’s Park (S54.5), then use a road portage to the next public launch; river immediately below the dam is not navigable and has no public access. Retain the existing park pin as the takeout/portage-area anchor.

controls.name: Taylors Falls Lions Park South dam portage take-out
aliases: Taylors Falls Lion's Park dam portage take-out
Lions Park South St. Croix access
controls.coordinateText: Existing point retained as the upstream-side portage takeout/park anchor; it is not a launch below the dam. NPS says the river below the dam is not navigable and has no public access.

providers.name: Sac County Grant Park North Raccoon boat-ramp access anchor
providers.method: The Sac County Grant Park listing confirms a hard-surface boat ramp to the North Raccoon River. The county/city water-trail map names Grant Park Access and shows the nearby rock dam; Iowa DNR project records document construction of the concrete ramp immediately downstream of the riffle. Keep the route coordinate as a park/ramp-area anchor rather than claiming an exact ramp toe or relying on park-centroid hydrography distance.

controls.name: Grant Park below-dam boat-ramp access area
aliases: Grant Park North Raccoon River access
controls.coordinateText: Stored route point is a Grant Park/ramp-area anchor; public hard-surface ramp is confirmed, but this is not an exact published ramp coordinate.

providers.name: Richmond Jonesville Winooski River takeout access anchor
providers.method: Richmond’s current river-access page identifies the Jonesville takeout just after the Cochran Road Bridge on river-left, says to unload on the shoulder, and directs vehicles to park opposite the bridge. Keep the existing point as a bridge/takeout access anchor; the Town does not publish a GPS coordinate for the landing and shoulder parking is distinct from the water entry.

controls.name: Jonesville Winooski River takeout below Cochran Road Bridge
aliases: Jonesville takeout below Cochran Road Bridge
controls.coordinateText: Stored endpoint retained as a road-bridge/takeout access anchor; unload below the bridge on river-left and park on the opposite side, subject to posted road/parking restrictions.
